accounts.name: market
docs: Mutable for `latest_maturity`, which a new epoch may move forward.

accounts.name: asset_mint
docs: The market's asset is a parameter, not a constant: no logic relies on
a specific mint or number of decimals (FR-001).

accounts.name: source_reserve
docs: Where the deterministic source's income physically comes from. Whoever runs the stand
funds it with a plain token transfer; `settle_epoch` pulls from it only what the
formula says the epoch earned, and only as much as is actually there.
Not a field on `Market`: its address follows from the seeds, and the account belongs
to the deterministic adapter rather than to the ladder core.

instructions.name: ladder_deposit
docs: Rungs arrive in `remaining_accounts`, so the context lifetime is named
explicitly here: otherwise the borrowed accounts would not outlive the call.

accounts.name: ladder
docs: `has_one = owner` is FR-020 itself: a foreign wallet sees the ladder but
has no path to put funds into it. `has_one = market` is deliberately left on
Anchor's built-in error: a mismatch here means a broken
client, not a treasurer's decision, and it gets no wording of its own.

accounts.name: buffer_vault
docs: The protocol buffer: the fee from the principal goes here (FR-023). It also stands
as the second step of the waterfall, so the fee is not funds leaving the system
but a top-up of what covers a shortfall.

accounts.name: source
docs: The wallet the funds leave from. It must belong to the ladder owner —
otherwise the treasurer's signature would debit someone else's account.

accounts.name: owner
docs: `Signer` checks exactly one thing — that the account signed the instruction. It does not
require the account to be owned by the system program, which is precisely why a multisig
safe signing through CPI is not a special case here (FR-020a).

accounts.name: ladder
docs: The owner is part of the seeds, so the address space is divided between owners:
a foreign signer cannot create a ladder at someone else's address — not because
a check catches it, but because the address is not derived from their key.

instructions.name: redeem_rung
docs: The owner signs; the funds go only to an account the owner controls (FR-012).

accounts.name: epoch
docs: Mutable for `redeemed`: the running total that keeps the epoch's redemptions inside what
it settled for.

accounts.name: rung
docs: The seeds bind the rung to this ladder, `has_one` to this epoch: a rung of another ladder
has a different address, and a rung of another epoch names that epoch. The epoch mismatch
stays on Anchor's built-in error, like `has_one = market` above — it means a broken
client, not an owner's decision.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Where the funds go. It must belong to the ladder owner — otherwise the owner's signature
would send the treasury's money to someone else's account.

instructions.name: roll_rung
docs: Permissionless: the new rung goes into the same ladder, and the epoch is the market's
furthest (FR-013).

accounts.name: payer
docs: Whoever sends the crank. Pays the rent of the new rung and nothing else; who it is does
not matter to the program.

accounts.name: ladder
docs: Mutable for `rung_count`. No `has_one = owner`: the owner does not sign here, and the
policy on the ladder is the owner's standing permission.

accounts.name: epoch
docs: The epoch the rung matured in. Mutable for `redeemed`, which counts rolled funds exactly
as it counts redeemed ones.

accounts.name: target
docs: The market's furthest epoch — the crank chooses neither the date nor the rate.

accounts.name: new_rung
docs: The ladder's next number, like any other rung it issues.

accounts.name: buffer_vault
docs: Where the issuance fee of the new rung goes — the only fee a roll takes (FR-024).

instructions.name: settle_epoch
docs: Permissionless: no signer, no destination, no amount (FR-011).

accounts.name: vault
docs: Where the epoch's principal sits, and where the source's income and the buffer's
contribution land.

accounts.name: buffer_vault
docs: The protocol buffer (FR-023). Its balance **is** the buffer in the waterfall — there is
no mirrored field to drift out of step with it, and moving the drawn amount out of it
here is what stops a second epoch from settling against money this one already used.

accounts.name: source_reserve
docs: The deterministic source's income, held as tokens. Checked by its seeds and not merely
by its owner: the vault and the buffer are owned by the market too, and passing the
vault here would count the epoch's own principal a second time as income.

errors.name: RungBelowMinimum
errors.msg: Rung is below the minimum position size — reduce the number of rungs or increase the amount

errors.name: InvalidFeeBps
errors.msg: Fee rate cannot exceed 100%

errors.name: InvalidMaturity
errors.msg: Maturity date must be in the future

errors.name: EpochAlreadyMatured
errors.msg: This maturity date has already passed — funds cannot be placed in it, choose the next one

errors.name: InvalidDistribution
errors.msg: Deposit layout is invalid: weights must add up to 10000 bps, and there must be at least one rung

errors.name: RungAccountsMismatch
errors.msg: Account set does not match the deposit layout: every rung needs its epoch and the rung itself

errors.name: ZeroAmount
errors.msg: Deposit amount must be greater than zero

errors.name: RateAlreadyLocked
errors.msg: Epoch rate is already locked — it is not revised after the first rung is issued

errors.name: EpochNotMatured
errors.msg: Epoch has not reached its maturity date yet

errors.name: EpochAlreadySettled
errors.msg: Epoch has already been settled

errors.name: EpochNotSettled
errors.msg: Epoch has not been settled yet — redemption becomes available after settlement

errors.name: NotLadderOwner
errors.msg: Only the ladder owner can perform this operation

errors.name: NotMarketAuthority
errors.msg: Only the market operator can create epochs

errors.name: InsufficientExitLiquidity
errors.msg: Not enough liquidity for an early exit — the position was left untouched

errors.name: RungNotActive
errors.msg: Rung has already been redeemed

errors.name: RollPolicyDisabled
errors.msg: Rolling is disabled for this ladder

errors.name: MathOverflow
errors.msg: Overflow in amount calculation

errors.name: RungExceedsEpochPromise
errors.msg: Rung promise is larger than its epoch's total — the epoch's accounting is inconsistent

errors.name: EpochOverpaid
errors.msg: Epoch would pay out more than it settled for — the epoch's accounting is inconsistent

errors.name: RollTargetNotLatest
errors.msg: Rolled funds go only into the market's furthest maturity date — pass that epoch

types.name: Distribution
docs: How the treasurer divides the amount between rungs.
A mirror of `Distribution` from `packages/math/src/ladder.ts`, and the even
split is just as much a separate variant here, not sugar over the weights
`[10000 / n, ...]`: for `n` that does not divide 10000 (3, 6, 7) such integer weights
do not exist, and a round-trip through bps would give a split that is called even
but is not. The dashboard shows the treasurer the preview with exactly that code, so a
discrepancy here is a different amount on screen and on chain.

types.name: Epoch
docs: A maturity epoch: one date and one rate for everyone who enters it.
The rate has no instruction that overwrites it — none. The invariant "a promise cannot
change after issuance" is held by the absence of a path, not by checking a flag:
to change the terms one would have to create another epoch, while rungs stay
bound to their own.

fields.name: created_by
docs: FR-010a: the operator is a conscious point of trust, so exactly who set
the rate and when lives in the account, not only in the transaction logs.

fields.name: total_deposited
docs: The amount that actually went to work across the whole epoch (after fees).

fields.name: total_promised
docs: The sum of promises across the whole epoch. Together with the funds available on the
maturity date it gives the payout ratio — one per epoch, not per rung.

fields.name: deposit_seconds
docs: `Σ(principal × seconds to maturity)` over the epoch's rungs, accumulated as they are
issued.
The epoch has no single `elapsed` to hand the source adapter: deposits arrive at
different moments and each rung earns over its own span. This one accumulator carries
exactly the quantity the accrual formula is linear in, so settlement stays **one
computation per epoch** instead of a walk over the rungs — which is the same bound
that puts the payout ratio here rather than on each rung.
`u128` because the product alone reaches `2^64` for large amounts over long spans.

fields.name: redeemed
docs: What its rungs have taken out of the vault so far. Never above `paid`: the vault is
shared by every epoch of the market, so a redemption past it would not fail — it would
pay out of another epoch's principal. The difference that remains once every rung is
redeemed is the rounding dust, which stays with the treasury side of the vault.

fields.name: status
docs: `Active` until the crank settles the epoch, then the payout ratio in union form.

types.name: EpochSettled
docs: The epoch settled: the one computation every rung in it will be paid by (FR-011).
`accrued` and `realized` are the reason this event exists. Neither survives in the account —
the status keeps only `paid` — and without them a deficit cannot be told apart from a
promise that was too large to begin with. That distinction is the difference between
"the market moved" and "the operator mispriced the epoch", and the treasurer is entitled
to it.

fields.name: accrued
docs: What the source owed over the epoch's `deposit_seconds`, by its formula.

fields.name: realized
docs: Principal plus what the source actually delivered: what the epoch had before the buffer
was asked. Below `principal + accrued` exactly when the source reserve ran short.

fields.name: paid
docs: Equals `promised` unless the buffer ran out first.

fields.name: from_buffer
docs: How much the protocol buffer covered — zero when the source covered the promise alone.

types.name: EpochStatus
docs: What happened to the epoch as a whole. A union rather than a status flag beside a
`payout_ratio` field: the pair would make "settled below the promise, unmarked"
representable, which is the one state FR-011a forbids — the same reasoning that shaped
`RungStatus`, applied one level up.
The variants carry `paid` rather than a ratio. A ratio would have to be a fixed-point
number chosen here and re-derived at every redemption, while `paid` together with
`total_promised` **is** the ratio, exactly as `math::payout` consumes it — and it is the
number a treasurer can check against the vault without trusting our rounding.

types.name: Ladder
docs: A ladder: a set of rungs of one owner on one market.
Ownership here is a `Pubkey` and nothing more. No field and no check
assumes a single private key stands behind this key: a multisig safe
takes the same path as an ordinary wallet (FR-020a).

fields.name: owner
docs: The only one who can initiate ladder operations (FR-020). A foreign wallet
reads the same accounts but has no path to change them.

fields.name: seed
docs: Distinguishes the ladders of one owner: a treasury keeps several —
for example, for different budget lines.

fields.name: rung_count
docs: How many rungs the ladder has issued over its lifetime. A counter, not a plan:
rolling (FR-013) adds rungs after the deposit, so any number declared
up front would drift from reality on the very first crank. It is also the number
the next rung takes in its seeds (`["rung", ladder, index]`).

types.name: LadderFunded
docs: The deposit summary. Rungs have events of their own, but the amount the treasurer
signed and the amount the protocol kept belong to none of them individually —
without this event they would have to be gathered by addition (FR-022).

fields.name: amount
docs: How much was debited from the treasury wallet — exactly what it confirmed.

fields.name: working_total
docs: How much of that went to work.

fields.name: withheld
docs: How much was kept in the protocol buffer.

fields.name: authority
docs: The operator: creates epochs and sets their rate. A conscious point of trust — see
`docs/SPEC.md`, FR-010a: who set the rate and when is visible to the treasurer.

fields.name: vault
docs: The vault for treasury deposits.

fields.name: buffer_vault
docs: The protocol buffer: filled by fees and standing as the second step of the
waterfall when the yield falls short (FR-011, FR-023).

fields.name: min_rung_amount
docs: The minimum rung size in the asset's smallest units (FR-006).
Lives on the market, not in the program and not in a deposit parameter: a constant
in base units means nothing without the mint's decimals (FR-001),
and a minimum the treasurer sets themselves protects against nothing. A meaningful
rung is one whose yield is not eaten by the network fee for redemption,
and the one who knows that is the market operator.

fields.name: latest_maturity
docs: The furthest maturity among the market's epochs — the only epoch `roll_rung` puts funds
into (FR-013). A running maximum kept by `create_epoch`, not the last one created: an
operator creating a shorter epoch afterwards must not pull every rolling ladder in with it.
Zero until the first epoch exists.

types.name: RollPolicy
docs: What happens to the rung's funds once it is redeemed.
The names come from `docs/PLAN.md` ("Flow: what happens on deposit"), where the policy
is referred to as `policy=Roll` and `policy=None`.

types.name: Rung
docs: A rung: one date, one fixed promise.
`promised` is written once, at creation. An instruction that overwrites it does not
exist — and this is not a flag check but the absence of a path: to change the terms
one would have to create another rung.
The address is `["rung", ladder, index]`, not `["rung", ladder, epoch]`: a ladder may hold
several rungs in one epoch — a second deposit, or a roll into an epoch the ladder already
uses (FR-013). The tie to the epoch is the `epoch` field, checked with `has_one`.

fields.name: index
docs: The rung's number within its ladder — the ladder's `rung_count` at the moment the rung
was issued. Kept in the account because it is part of the seeds: without it, an
instruction taking this rung could not check its address.

fields.name: deposited
docs: How much actually went to work — the amount after the protocol fee.

fields.name: promised
docs: How much the treasury receives on the maturity date. The same number the treasurer
saw in the deposit preview (FR-007).

types.name: RungIssued
docs: One rung at the moment of issuance. `promised` here is the same number that landed in
the account and will never change: the event fixes the promise in time rather than
relaying current state.

types.name: RungRedeemed
docs: One rung redeemed (FR-015: when, how much, and where the funds went).
`with_deficit` is explicit rather than left to `amount < promised`: under a deficit a rung
promised nothing receives nothing, which compares equal and would read as "paid in full".

types.name: RungRolled
docs: One rung rolled by the crank (FR-013, FR-015: where the funds went). The new rung has its own
`RungIssued` in the same transaction; this event is the link between the two, and the only
place the old rung's payout and the destination appear together.

fields.name: into
docs: The new rung the funds went into.

types.name: RungStatus
docs: What happened to the rung. A union rather than a sum of boolean flags: the variant
"redeemed for less than promised, unmarked" does not exist in the type, so a deficit cannot
become silent through a forgotten check (FR-011a).
The actual amount lives in the variant, not in a separate field, and this is a deliberate
departure from the table in `docs/PLAN.md`: a `settled_amount` field next to the status would
give exactly the representability the invariant forbids.

types.name: YieldSource
docs: Which base yield source serves the market and with what parameters.
The behaviour lives behind the adapter boundary in `source/`, and the ladder core does not know it.
